newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel denies any military involvement in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Israel denies any military involvement in Zaire.

text.p: Israel denied on Thursday any military involvement in Zaire's campaign to stop advances by Tutsi-led rebels in its east.
A Zairean defence official said on Monday that Israel and China would help train army commandos at bases in the Zaire provinces of Shaba, Upper Zaire and Equateur.

"Following press reports about alleged Israeli military involvement in Zaire, the spokesman of the (Israeli) Foreign Ministry denies any such involvement on the part of Israel," the ministry said in a statement.
Rebels battling the Zaire army since October have extended their campaign and territory they hold from the borders of Rwanda and Uganda to Zaire's mineral-rich Shaba Province.
Zaire has said it was expecting troops from Togo, Chad and Morocco as well as material assistance from Egypt.
Togo denied planning to send troops. Egypt said it had no defence ties with Zaire. There was no word from Chad or Morocco, which Zaire's veteran ruler Mobutu Sese Seko is visiting.
The United States said on Wednesday it had urged Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi to stay out of fighting in eastern Zaire.
